final_candidate.name: steric_pair_to_included_sphere_ratio
final_candidate.hypothesis: If confinement-driven rotational entropy loss dominates for these molecule-framework pairs, then, holding the framework geometry fixed (lsd_p fixed), an adsorbate with a larger heavy-atom pair distance (GeDi, longest molecular dimension proxy) loses a larger fraction of its gas-phase entropy on adsorption; and, holding the adsorbate fixed, a framework with a larger included sphere along the free-sphere path (lsd_p) imposes a smaller entropy loss. The descriptor GeDi/lsd_p is a dimensionless steric-confinement ratio expected to increase with entropy_loss_over_R=(Sgas-Sads)/R.
final_candidate.rationale: Evidence E02 reports that smaller-cavity zeolites (FER vs FAU) show larger rotational entropy loss, and E01/E04 report larger entropy loss in MFI than FAU. The present inputs do not contain the global cavity diameter Di; lsd_p (Zeo++ Dif) is only the largest included sphere along the free-sphere path and is used here as an empirical proxy for local confinement space, which is a weaker quantity than Di. GeDi is a heavy-atom pair distance in an implicit-H representation, not the full all-atom longest dimension including hydrogens; for single-site molecules GeDi is a legitimate native zero, giving descriptor value 0. This is a proxy combination, not a measured degree-of-freedom count; the descriptor re-expresses existing D0 information rather than adding an observation.
final_candidate.falsification_criteria: The hypothesis fails if, within the training support, pairs with high GeDi/lsd_p do not exhibit higher entropy loss than pairs with low GeDi/lsd_p at comparable AV/ASA (i.e., the apparent relation is explained by accessibility rather than confinement), or if single-site adsorbates (GeDi=0, descriptor 0) do not rank among the lower entropy-loss cases at fixed lsd_p. A competing explanation is that lsd_p correlates with accessible volume (AV) and the mechanism is translational rather than rotational; if including AV removes the descriptor's contribution, the rotational-confinement interpretation is unsupported.
final_candidate.proxy_assumptions: Assumes lsd_p (Dif, included-along-path sphere) monotonically proxies the local confinement space relevant to rotational freedom, which is not the global cavity diameter Di and not the bottleneck Df. Assumes GeDi (implicit-H heavy-atom pair distance) proxies the molecular dimension relevant to rotational restriction. Assumes infinite-dilution, pure-silica-like rigid-framework transfer from the reported zeolite comparisons (C1, C2, C4). No fitted source coefficient is used; the ratio is dimensionless and native.
final_candidate.boundary_behavior: Finite training support: GeDi in [0, 10.97181443] angstrom (legitimate native zeros for 54 single-site molecules preserved, giving descriptor 0), lsd_p in [3.3452, 15.5604] angstrom (strictly positive, so the ratio is defined everywhere in the training domain). No median imputation and no log applied, so native zeros are not distorted.

Given the constraints of a fixed number of molecules (N), volume (V), and temperature (T), it is natural to continue working in the canonical ensemble. However, performing experiments for many molecule-framework combinations is impractical. Computational experiments of adsorption therefore make for an attractive alternative. Nevertheless, there remain caveats. For example, quantifying the entropy using ab initio-based methods (such as density functional theory) is computationally demanding $ ^{18-22} $ or relies on approximations. $ ^{19} $ Such approximations include (1) limiting translation to the surface area of the zeolite, $ ^{23} $ which artificially restricts the entropy to a surface term; (2) invocation of the “harmonic approximation” based on the assumption of a very strong fluid–solid interaction that renders translations and rotations unimportant; or (3) employing the hindered translator/rotor model. $ ^{24} $ On the other hand, (classical) Monte Carlo (MC) and molecular dynamics simulations have proven successful in accurately calculating the adsorption entropy, $ ^{25} $ with the primary limitation being the number of force fields available to accurately model the adsorbate–adsorbent interaction. review_issues.explanation: Proxy mismatch for the confinement quantity: evidence E02 explicitly uses 'average cavity diameter' (FER ~4.3 A vs FAU ~13 A) as the confinement descriptor, but the input set contains no global cavity diameter Di. The draft substitutes lsd_p, which per its own definition is the largest included sphere ALONG the free-sphere path (Zeo++ Dif), explicitly 'NOT necessarily global cavity Di'. The mapping Dif -> cavity-diameter-like confinement space is an empirical substitution that is weaker than the source quantity and must be justified, not assumed. The relation facts grant only MAY_USE_PROXY_UNDER_ASSUMPTIONS status, and the diameter_roles definition constraint flags exactly this distinction.

Adsorbate-size proxy is representation-limited: GeDi is the largest distance between two heavy atoms in an implicit-H/heavy-atom representation. It is not the full all-atom longest molecular dimension (hydrogen-inclusive extent), so the numerator does not measure the steric dimension of the actual adsorbing molecule. Legitimate native zeros (54 single-site molecules, GeDi=0) force the descriptor to exactly 0 for monoatomic/single-site adsorbates regardless of framework, so the ratio conflates 'no heavy-atom pair distance' with 'no confinement-relevant size'. This is a definitional artifact of the representation, not a physical claim that single-site species experience no confinement.

The ratio GeDi/lsd_p is dimensionless, but dimensionless does not confer a physical threshold: per the normalization caveat, a native ratio value of 1 (GeDi equal to the included-sphere diameter) is not a known equality or transition condition for rotational freedom. The hypothesis asserts monotonic increase of entropy_loss_over_R with the ratio without any stated or verifiable scale at which confinement switches character; this ordering claim is an empirical choice, not a derived physical relation.

The draft's own structured limit test fails: for vary_input=GeDi approaching positive infinity the expected_value is 0.0 but the computed limit is infinity (status: failed, recorded as scientific issue 'Incorrect structured limit: GeDi'). Since lsd_p is held finite in that test, GeDi/lsd_p diverges, contradicting the recorded boundary expectation. The boundary_behavior narrative and the limit_tests block are internally inconsistent for the GeDi branch and cannot both stand as preservation records.

Extrapolation beyond training support: the lsd_p -> positive_infinity limit (descriptor -> 0) has no counterpart in the training domain, where lsd_p spans only [3.3452, 15.5604] A. The limit behavior is asserted for a regime with zero training support and cannot be validated by the data; it should be recorded as untested extrapolation, not as a verified property.

The mechanism attribution to rotation is underdetermined by the descriptor: the cited mechanisms (E01, E02, E04) concern loss of rotational degrees of freedom/rotational entropy, but GeDi/lsd_p encodes only a steric size-vs-space ratio and contains no rotational-inertia information (no PMI1/PMI2/PMI3, no rotor_case branch). A larger molecule with larger GeDi would also have reduced translational freedom; the same descriptor is equally consistent with a translational-confinement mechanism. The falsification criteria acknowledge this competing explanation (AV correlation) but it remains unresolved; mechanism_validated is false and the mechanism card is conditional, so the rotational interpretation is a hypothesis, not a demonstrated cause.

Unverified prediction for single-site adsorbates: the hypothesis implies descriptor 0 (GeDi=0) corresponds to minimal entropy loss, and the falsification criterion requires single-site species to rank among lower entropy-loss cases at fixed lsd_p. For a single-site adsorbate (e.g., a spherical atom), confinement loss is predominantly translational, not rotational, so the descriptor being 0 does not follow from any cited mechanism; this prediction for the GeDi=0 branch is an untested extrapolation of the source evidence, which concerned alkanes (linear/branched molecules), not single-site species.

Transfer conditions are unresolved in the sources: E01/E02/E04 are reported comparisons in specific zeolites (MFI, FAU, FER) for linear alkanes with temperature, loading, and framework chemistry not fully resolved in the excerpts; E04's quoted percentages (38% vs 20%) are source-specific and must not become universal constants. Transfer to infinite dilution and pure-silica-like rigid frameworks at benchmark conditions remains a hypothesis (per source_conditions C1, C2, C4), so the sign/direction claim of the descriptor is conditionally supported only.

No source supplies the ratio form: the cited evidence motivates confinement-entropy associations qualitatively; none of E01, E02, E04 provides a GeDi/lsd_p-type combination or any coefficient. The specific functional form is a new combination proposed by the draft; its novelty and validity are not attested by any evidence item, and prior_formulas is empty.

Graph support is incomplete: the knowledge graph grants proxy edges from the rotational-confinement mechanisms to lsd_p and GeDi only under stated assumptions, and the note states these are conditional proxy assumptions, not causal edges or executed check results. Absence of additional edges (e.g., linking the ratio itself, or AV-mediated translational pathways, to the target) is unknown support, not disproof; the causal chain from descriptor to entropy_loss_over_R remains unverified and should be preserved as unresolved rather than treated as confirmed or refuted.

final_candidate.hypothesis: If translational/configurational confinement at the framework bottleneck dominates the entropy loss for these molecule-framework pairs, then, holding the framework geometry fixed (lsd_f fixed), an adsorbate with a larger heavy-atom enclosing radius (SPAN) sweeps out a larger excluded volume near the pore windows and its adsorbed-phase translational/configurational freedom is more restricted, giving a larger entropy loss; and, holding the adsorbate fixed, a framework with a larger passing free-sphere diameter (lsd_f) permits more translational mobility, giving a smaller entropy loss. The dimensionless squared ratio (SPAN/lsd_f)^2 is therefore expected to increase with entropy_loss_over_R=(Sgas-Sads)/R. This is a falsifiable conditional statement motivated by the reported FER/FAU and MFI/FAU confinement comparisons (E01, E02, E04), not an established law.
final_candidate.rationale: Proxy limitations: SPAN is a heavy-atom enclosing radius in the implicit-H representation (legitimate zero for single-site species, e.g., 54 training rows) and is not an all-atom molecular size; lsd_f is Zeo++ Df, the largest sphere that can PASS through a periodic free path — a bottleneck diameter, not the global cavity diameter Di (E02's cavity-diameter mechanism must be mapped through this bottleneck proxy explicitly, which is unverified). The square gives a cross-section-like dimensionless ratio (molecular enclosing radius vs. bottleneck radius) but does not preserve any physical equality threshold at 1: SPAN > lsd_f does not prove the molecule cannot transit the pore, because SPAN is a heavy-atom radius about the center of mass while Df is a geometric free-sphere path along the framework. Mechanistically the descriptor couples an adsorbate size/shape proxy with a framework transport-limiting length, targeting the translational side of the reported translational-plus-rotational entropy loss picture (E03). It is distinct from the round-1 descriptor GeDi/lsd_p, which paired a molecular pair-distance with the included-along-path sphere.
final_candidate.falsification_criteria: The hypothesis is falsified if: (1) entropy_loss_over_R does not increase with (SPAN/lsd_f)^2 within frameworks of similar chemistry when other size proxies (Vol, GeDi, MW) are held fixed; (2) the framework bottleneck term adds nothing, i.e., SPAN alone (or lsd_f alone with the adsorbate varied) explains the same variation, indicating the ratio is redundant rather than capturing a confinement coupling; (3) the loss instead tracks the included-along-path sphere lsd_p (cage size) rather than the passing bottleneck lsd_f, supporting a cavity-volume mechanism over a window-bottleneck mechanism.
final_candidate.proxy_assumptions: Assumptions (not established causality): (a) the heavy-atom enclosing radius SPAN is an adequate surrogate for the molecular sweep radius governing translational/configurational restriction in a pore; (b) the passing free-sphere diameter Df is an adequate bottleneck-side surrogate for the confinement length, even though the reported mechanism (E02) used average cavity diameter, which is a different geometric quantity; (c) the confinement-driven entropy-loss mechanism reported for alkanes in MFI/FER vs FAU transfers to this benchmark's molecule-framework pairs at its operating conditions; (d) the squared ratio is a monotone empirical proxy, not a physical cross-section model, and ratio=1 has no threshold meaning.
final_candidate.boundary_behavior: Finite training support: SPAN in [0, 6.2408] angstrom with legitimate physical zeros (54 single-site rows) preserved — the descriptor is exactly 0 there and no imputation is applied; lsd_f in [0.85684, 7.68726] angstrom is strictly positive in training, so the ratio has no division-by-zero within the observed domain; the descriptor is non-negative and finite wherever lsd_f > 0. Native zeros of SPAN are not converted to reference values.

Given the constraints of a fixed number of molecules (N), volume (V), and temperature (T), it is natural to continue working in the canonical ensemble. However, performing experiments for many molecule-framework combinations is impractical. Computational experiments of adsorption therefore make for an attractive alternative. Nevertheless, there remain caveats. For example, quantifying the entropy using ab initio-based methods (such as density functional theory) is computationally demanding $ ^{18-22} $ or relies on approximations. $ ^{19} $ Such approximations include (1) limiting translation to the surface area of the zeolite, $ ^{23} $ which artificially restricts the entropy to a surface term; (2) invocation of the “harmonic approximation” based on the assumption of a very strong fluid–solid interaction that renders translations and rotations unimportant; or (3) employing the hindered translator/rotor model. $ ^{24} $ On the other hand, (classical) Monte Carlo (MC) and molecular dynamics simulations have proven successful in accurately calculating the adsorption entropy, $ ^{25} $ with the primary limitation being the number of force fields available to accurately model the adsorbate–adsorbent interaction. In the following appendix , we derive the entropy of adsorption in the case of infinite dilution and show how it may be related to familiar thermodynamic quantities ( cf . eq 5 ) . To begin , we define our adsorption entropy in the limit of infinite dilution via $$ \Delta s_{\mathrm{ads}}^{\infty}=\lim_{N/V\rightarrow0}\left[\left(\frac{\partial S}{\partial N}\right)_{V,T,\mathrm{ads}}-\left(\frac{\partial S}{\partial N}\right)_{V,T,\mathrm{gas}}\right] $$ $$ =S_{ads}(N=1,V,T)-S_{gas}(N=1,V,T) $$ where the subscripts “ads” and “gas” labels identify the adsorbed (confined) and gas (bulk) phases, respectively. Given the constraints of a fixed number of molecules (N), volume (V), and temperature (T), it is natural to continue working in the canonical ensemble. (As in the main text, lowercase symbols identify intensive molecular or molar properties, whereas the uppercase indicates an extensive property.) For the molecules that we examine in this work (e.g., rigid molecules with no internal degrees of freedom), the canonical partition function Q may be expressed as $$ \begin{aligned}Q(N,V,T)&=Q_{trans}(N,V,T)Q_{rot}(N,V,T)\\&\quad\times Z(N,V,T)\end{aligned} $$ where $ Q_{trans} $ and $ Q_{rot} $ are the translational and rotational partition functions (which are unaffected by confinement) and Z is the configurational partition function. The translational and rotational partition functions are available in the usual statistical mechanics texts $ ^{44,45} $ but are ultimately unimportant for the derivation that follows. However, performing experiments for many molecule-framework combinations is impractical. Computational experiments of adsorption therefore make for an attractive alternative. Nevertheless, there remain caveats. For example, quantifying the entropy using ab initio-based methods (such as density functional theory) is computationally demanding $ ^{18-22} $ or relies on approximations. $ ^{19} $ Such approximations include (1) limiting translation to the surface area of the zeolite, $ ^{23} $ which artificially restricts the entropy to a surface term; (2) invocation of the “harmonic approximation” based on the assumption of a very strong fluid–solid interaction that renders translations and rotations unimportant; or (3) employing the hindered translator/rotor model. $ ^{24} $ On the other hand, (classical) Monte Carlo (MC) and molecular dynamics simulations have proven successful in accurately calculating the adsorption entropy, $ ^{25} $ with the primary limitation being the number of force fields available to accurately model the adsorbate–adsorbent interaction. Although these simulations are numerically cleaner compared to experiment because they involve analyzing efficiently a greater number of molecule–zeolite combinations, it remains overwhelming to apply them to the millions of hypothetical frameworks. Novel topology-based, data-driven approaches have been shown to be adequate in predicting specific features such as adsorption capacity $ ^{6} $ and selectivity. $ ^{26} $ However, there are currently no similar models for entropy.

draft.name: bottleneck_confinement_ratio_sq
draft.hypothesis: If translational/configurational confinement at the framework bottleneck dominates the entropy loss for these molecule-framework pairs, then, holding the framework geometry fixed (lsd_f fixed), an adsorbate with a larger heavy-atom enclosing radius (SPAN) sweeps out a larger excluded volume near the pore windows and its adsorbed-phase translational/configurational freedom is more restricted, giving a larger entropy loss; and, holding the adsorbate fixed, a framework with a larger passing free-sphere diameter (lsd_f) permits more translational mobility, giving a smaller entropy loss. The dimensionless squared ratio (SPAN/lsd_f)^2 is therefore expected to increase with entropy_loss_over_R=(Sgas-Sads)/R. This is a falsifiable conditional statement motivated by the reported FER/FAU and MFI/FAU confinement comparisons (E01, E02, E04), not an established law.
draft.rationale: Proxy limitations: SPAN is a heavy-atom enclosing radius in the implicit-H representation (legitimate zero for single-site species, e.g., 54 training rows) and is not an all-atom molecular size; lsd_f is Zeo++ Df, the largest sphere that can PASS through a periodic free path — a bottleneck diameter, not the global cavity diameter Di (E02's cavity-diameter mechanism must be mapped through this bottleneck proxy explicitly, which is unverified). The square gives a cross-section-like dimensionless ratio (molecular enclosing radius vs. bottleneck radius) but does not preserve any physical equality threshold at 1: SPAN > lsd_f does not prove the molecule cannot transit the pore, because SPAN is a heavy-atom radius about the center of mass while Df is a geometric free-sphere path along the framework. Mechanistically the descriptor couples an adsorbate size/shape proxy with a framework transport-limiting length, targeting the translational side of the reported translational-plus-rotational entropy loss picture (E03). It is distinct from the round-1 descriptor GeDi/lsd_p, which paired a molecular pair-distance with the included-along-path sphere.
draft.falsification_criteria: The hypothesis is falsified if: (1) entropy_loss_over_R does not increase with (SPAN/lsd_f)^2 within frameworks of similar chemistry when other size proxies (Vol, GeDi, MW) are held fixed; (2) the framework bottleneck term adds nothing, i.e., SPAN alone (or lsd_f alone with the adsorbate varied) explains the same variation, indicating the ratio is redundant rather than capturing a confinement coupling; (3) the loss instead tracks the included-along-path sphere lsd_p (cage size) rather than the passing bottleneck lsd_f, supporting a cavity-volume mechanism over a window-bottleneck mechanism.
draft.proxy_assumptions: Assumptions (not established causality): (a) the heavy-atom enclosing radius SPAN is an adequate surrogate for the molecular sweep radius governing translational/configurational restriction in a pore; (b) the passing free-sphere diameter Df is an adequate bottleneck-side surrogate for the confinement length, even though the reported mechanism (E02) used average cavity diameter, which is a different geometric quantity; (c) the confinement-driven entropy-loss mechanism reported for alkanes in MFI/FER vs FAU transfers to this benchmark's molecule-framework pairs at its operating conditions; (d) the squared ratio is a monotone empirical proxy, not a physical cross-section model, and ratio=1 has no threshold meaning.
draft.boundary_behavior: Finite training support: SPAN in [0, 6.2408] angstrom with legitimate physical zeros (54 single-site rows) preserved — the descriptor is exactly 0 there and no imputation is applied; lsd_f in [0.85684, 7.68726] angstrom is strictly positive in training, so the ratio has no division-by-zero within the observed domain; the descriptor is non-negative and finite wherever lsd_f > 0. Native zeros of SPAN are not converted to reference values.

review_issues.explanation: Radius-vs-diameter ambiguity: the input defines lsd_f as the 'largest sphere able to pass through a periodic free path' without stating whether the reported number is a radius or a diameter, while SPAN is explicitly a radius about the center of mass. The draft labels lsd_f a 'passing free-sphere diameter' and forms SPAN/lsd_f; if the stored Zeo++ Df value is a diameter, the ratio mixes a molecular radius with a pore diameter, introducing an unstated factor-of-2 asymmetry. This must be resolved from the descriptor's native convention before any geometric interpretation of the ratio is asserted.

Representation mismatch between numerator and denominator: SPAN is computed on the implicit-H/heavy-atom representation (legitimate zeros, 54 single-site training rows) and encloses heavy-atom positions about the center of mass, whereas Df is a geometric free-sphere path quantity of the framework defined against a fixed probe. The two lengths are not measured on comparable molecular objects; the ratio is a heuristic dimensionless combination, and the draft's 'cross-section-like' reading of the square is an analogy, not a derived quantity. The draft acknowledges this, but the review records that the analogy is unverified.

The squared ratio has no preserved threshold at 1: SPAN > lsd_f does not imply the molecule cannot pass the bottleneck, because SPAN is an enclosing radius of heavy atoms about the COM while Df is defined along a periodic diffusion path with a probe sphere. The draft states this; the issue is recorded here so that no downstream use treats ratio >= 1 or the square as a physical confinement criterion.

Degenerate branch at SPAN = 0: for the 54 single-site training rows the descriptor is identically 0 regardless of lsd_f. On this branch the framework term carries no information, the derivative with respect to lsd_f is zero, and the descriptor cannot distinguish frameworks at all for these adsorbates. This is a legitimate preserved physical zero (no imputation applied, consistent with the stated rules), but the hypothesis 'larger SPAN -> larger loss, smaller lsd_f -> larger loss' is vacuous rather than confirmed on these rows, and near-zero-but-nonzero SPAN values (e.g., linear species with small PBF/PMI1 near zero) make the descriptor extremely nonlinear near the origin. The derivative check (nonzero_fraction 1.0, perturbation 0.0216) does not report how the perturbation interacts with the SPAN=0 boundary.

Evidence-mechanism mismatch (rotational vs translational): the cited comparisons E01, E02, and E04 report losses of ROTATIONAL degrees of freedom / rotational entropy (MFI vs FAU, FER vs FAU by cavity diameter); only E03 mentions translational and rotational losses jointly. The draft assigns mechanism_family 'translation' and attributes the effect to translational/configurational restriction at bottleneck windows. Mapping rotational-entropy evidence onto a bottleneck-Df translational mechanism is an extrapolation not contained in any cited source, and the draft's own rationale concedes the E02 cavity-diameter mechanism 'must be mapped through this bottleneck proxy explicitly, which is unverified.'

Geometric proxy mismatch with the source descriptor: E02 explicitly uses average cavity diameter as the confinement descriptor ('the average cavity diameter is a descriptor ... indicates the extent of confinement'). Neither lsd_f (Df, passing bottleneck) nor lsd_p (Dif, included along path) is the average cavity diameter Di; the knowledge-base constraint diameter_roles states neither is global Di. The draft uses Df, the quantity most different from the source's cavity diameter, so the conditional mechanism transfer rests on a double proxy substitution (cavity diameter -> bottleneck free sphere, rotational -> translational freedom), each unverified.

Source-scope transfer is conditional: E01/E04 concern linear alkanes in MFI/FAU at unspecified temperature and loading; E02 concerns FER vs FAU. The benchmark spans 2361 molecule-framework pairs with adsorbates up to MW 184 and frameworks whose chemistry is not resolved in the excerpts. The draft labels the statement conditional and falsifiable, which is appropriate; this review records that no cited source demonstrates the (SPAN/lsd_f)^2 relation, and source-specific percentages (38%, 20%, 3-fold) must not enter any coefficient or threshold.

Unverified mechanism language in the hypothesis: 'sweeps out a larger excluded volume near the pore windows' and 'permits more translational mobility' are proposed pictures, not established effects; SPAN about the center of mass is not a collision or excluded-volume radius, and Df along a periodic path is not demonstrated to govern adsorbed-phase mobility for this dataset. The hypothesis is retained as a falsifiable conditional claim; causality is not established by the execution checks (derivative sign consistency over the training domain only shows monotonicity of the formula, not of the entropy loss).

Conditional prediction holds only lsd_f fixed while varying SPAN. lsd_f alone does not fix the framework: co-varying framework quantities (ASA, AV, density, lsd_p) are not held fixed and are not used in the formula, so the conditional statement is internally consistent with the formula rules, but empirically SPAN covaries with other adsorbate size descriptors (GeDi, Vol, MW); the falsification criterion (1) partially addresses this by holding Vol/GeDi/MW fixed. The single-variable physical prediction should not be read as an isolated causal effect of molecular size.

Support and scale: the descriptor is finite and positive wherever lsd_f > 0 (lsd_f strictly positive in training, min 0.85684 angstrom), so no division-by-zero within the observed domain. However, the ratio spans a wide empirical range (SPAN/lsd_f from 0 to about 6.24/0.857 ~ 7.3, squared up to ~53), and the limit test only covers lsd_f -> infinity (descriptor -> 0); behavior as lsd_f approaches its lower training bound is dominated by the largest adsorbates and is untested. Extrapolation beyond the training quantiles is unsupported.

The derivative check (opposite_n 0, nonzero_fraction 1.0, regime_n 2361, perturbation 0.0216 on SPAN) verifies only uniform sign of d(descriptor)/d(SPAN) under a single perturbation size. It does not probe the lsd_f direction, the SPAN=0 boundary rows (where the descriptor is flat in lsd_f), or sensitivity of the sign conclusion to perturbation magnitude. This is a limitation of the check, not evidence against the descriptor.

Relation to the round-1 descriptor GeDi/lsd_p is unresolved: both are molecular-length / framework-length ratios differing in numerator (GeDi vs SPAN) and framework side (Dif vs Df). They are not duplicates under the stated rule, but their empirical correlation and whether Df vs Df-path distinctions carry separable information are unknown; absent graph edges or statistics on this redundancy are unknown, not disproof of either mechanism. Falsification criterion (3) proposes discriminating Df vs lsd_p mechanistically, but no data here confirm that discrimination is possible.

Whether the confinement mechanism reported for zeolites (E01, E02, E04) transfers to the benchmark's frameworks and operating conditions (temperature, loading, framework chemistry) is unresolved in the excerpts; all transfer assumptions are recorded as hypotheses. Absent knowledge-graph edges linking SPAN to translational entropy loss are unknown, not evidence against the proxy.

review_issues.explanation: Radius-vs-diameter ambiguity: the input defines lsd_f as the 'largest sphere able to pass through a periodic free path' without stating whether the reported number is a radius or a diameter, while SPAN is explicitly a radius about the center of mass. The draft labels lsd_f a 'passing free-sphere diameter' and forms SPAN/lsd_f; if the stored Zeo++ Df value is a diameter, the ratio mixes a molecular radius with a pore diameter, introducing an unstated factor-of-2 asymmetry. This must be resolved from the descriptor's native convention before any geometric interpretation of the ratio is asserted.

Representation mismatch between numerator and denominator: SPAN is computed on the implicit-H/heavy-atom representation (legitimate zeros, 54 single-site training rows) and encloses heavy-atom positions about the center of mass, whereas Df is a geometric free-sphere path quantity of the framework defined against a fixed probe. The two lengths are not measured on comparable molecular objects; the ratio is a heuristic dimensionless combination, and the draft's 'cross-section-like' reading of the square is an analogy, not a derived quantity. The draft acknowledges this, but the review records that the analogy is unverified.

The squared ratio has no preserved threshold at 1: SPAN > lsd_f does not imply the molecule cannot pass the bottleneck, because SPAN is an enclosing radius of heavy atoms about the COM while Df is defined along a periodic diffusion path with a probe sphere. The draft states this; the issue is recorded here so that no downstream use treats ratio >= 1 or the square as a physical confinement criterion.

Degenerate branch at SPAN = 0: for the 54 single-site training rows the descriptor is identically 0 regardless of lsd_f. On this branch the framework term carries no information, the derivative with respect to lsd_f is zero, and the descriptor cannot distinguish frameworks at all for these adsorbates. This is a legitimate preserved physical zero (no imputation applied, consistent with the stated rules), but the hypothesis 'larger SPAN -> larger loss, smaller lsd_f -> larger loss' is vacuous rather than confirmed on these rows, and near-zero-but-nonzero SPAN values (e.g., linear species with small PBF/PMI1 near zero) make the descriptor extremely nonlinear near the origin. The derivative check (nonzero_fraction 1.0, perturbation 0.0216) does not report how the perturbation interacts with the SPAN=0 boundary.

Evidence-mechanism mismatch (rotational vs translational): the cited comparisons E01, E02, and E04 report losses of ROTATIONAL degrees of freedom / rotational entropy (MFI vs FAU, FER vs FAU by cavity diameter); only E03 mentions translational and rotational losses jointly. The draft assigns mechanism_family 'translation' and attributes the effect to translational/configurational restriction at bottleneck windows. Mapping rotational-entropy evidence onto a bottleneck-Df translational mechanism is an extrapolation not contained in any cited source, and the draft's own rationale concedes the E02 cavity-diameter mechanism 'must be mapped through this bottleneck proxy explicitly, which is unverified.'

Geometric proxy mismatch with the source descriptor: E02 explicitly uses average cavity diameter as the confinement descriptor ('the average cavity diameter is a descriptor ... indicates the extent of confinement'). Neither lsd_f (Df, passing bottleneck) nor lsd_p (Dif, included along path) is the average cavity diameter Di; the knowledge-base constraint diameter_roles states neither is global Di. The draft uses Df, the quantity most different from the source's cavity diameter, so the conditional mechanism transfer rests on a double proxy substitution (cavity diameter -> bottleneck free sphere, rotational -> translational freedom), each unverified.

Source-scope transfer is conditional: E01/E04 concern linear alkanes in MFI/FAU at unspecified temperature and loading; E02 concerns FER vs FAU. The benchmark spans 2361 molecule-framework pairs with adsorbates up to MW 184 and frameworks whose chemistry is not resolved in the excerpts. The draft labels the statement conditional and falsifiable, which is appropriate; this review records that no cited source demonstrates the (SPAN/lsd_f)^2 relation, and source-specific percentages (38%, 20%, 3-fold) must not enter any coefficient or threshold.

Unverified mechanism language in the hypothesis: 'sweeps out a larger excluded volume near the pore windows' and 'permits more translational mobility' are proposed pictures, not established effects; SPAN about the center of mass is not a collision or excluded-volume radius, and Df along a periodic path is not demonstrated to govern adsorbed-phase mobility for this dataset. The hypothesis is retained as a falsifiable conditional claim; causality is not established by the execution checks (derivative sign consistency over the training domain only shows monotonicity of the formula, not of the entropy loss).

Conditional prediction holds only lsd_f fixed while varying SPAN. lsd_f alone does not fix the framework: co-varying framework quantities (ASA, AV, density, lsd_p) are not held fixed and are not used in the formula, so the conditional statement is internally consistent with the formula rules, but empirically SPAN covaries with other adsorbate size descriptors (GeDi, Vol, MW); the falsification criterion (1) partially addresses this by holding Vol/GeDi/MW fixed. The single-variable physical prediction should not be read as an isolated causal effect of molecular size.

Support and scale: the descriptor is finite and positive wherever lsd_f > 0 (lsd_f strictly positive in training, min 0.85684 angstrom), so no division-by-zero within the observed domain. However, the ratio spans a wide empirical range (SPAN/lsd_f from 0 to about 6.24/0.857 ~ 7.3, squared up to ~53), and the limit test only covers lsd_f -> infinity (descriptor -> 0); behavior as lsd_f approaches its lower training bound is dominated by the largest adsorbates and is untested. Extrapolation beyond the training quantiles is unsupported.

The derivative check (opposite_n 0, nonzero_fraction 1.0, regime_n 2361, perturbation 0.0216 on SPAN) verifies only uniform sign of d(descriptor)/d(SPAN) under a single perturbation size. It does not probe the lsd_f direction, the SPAN=0 boundary rows (where the descriptor is flat in lsd_f), or sensitivity of the sign conclusion to perturbation magnitude. This is a limitation of the check, not evidence against the descriptor.

Relation to the round-1 descriptor GeDi/lsd_p is unresolved: both are molecular-length / framework-length ratios differing in numerator (GeDi vs SPAN) and framework side (Dif vs Df). They are not duplicates under the stated rule, but their empirical correlation and whether Df vs Df-path distinctions carry separable information are unknown; absent graph edges or statistics on this redundancy are unknown, not disproof of either mechanism. Falsification criterion (3) proposes discriminating Df vs lsd_p mechanistically, but no data here confirm that discrimination is possible.

Whether the confinement mechanism reported for zeolites (E01, E02, E04) transfers to the benchmark's frameworks and operating conditions (temperature, loading, framework chemistry) is unresolved in the excerpts; all transfer assumptions are recorded as hypotheses. Absent knowledge-graph edges linking SPAN to translational entropy loss are unknown, not evidence against the proxy.

final_candidate.name: vol_to_included_sphere_packing_ratio
final_candidate.hypothesis: If configurational packing confinement dominates the entropy loss for these molecule-framework pairs, then, holding the framework geometry fixed (lsd_p fixed), an adsorbate with a larger van der Waals volume (Vol) excludes a larger fraction of the included-sphere volume along the free-sphere path, leaving fewer accessible positional/orientational microstates in the adsorbed phase and thus a larger entropy loss; and, holding the adsorbate fixed, a framework with a larger included sphere along the free-sphere path (lsd_p) accommodates more positional and orientational configurations, giving a smaller entropy loss. The dimensionless packing ratio Vol/lsd_p**3 is therefore expected to increase with entropy_loss_over_R=(Sgas-Sads)/R.
final_candidate.rationale: Prior descriptors captured linear confinement (GeDi/lsd_p, rotation proxy) and bottleneck cross-section confinement ((SPAN/lsd_f)**2, translation proxy). This descriptor probes the volumetric (three-dimensional packing) degree of confinement: how much of the largest included sphere along the diffusion path the molecule's vdW volume occupies. Vol is a computed vdW volume of the implicit-H molecule, not a measured free volume; lsd_p is the Zeo++ Dif (largest included sphere along the free-sphere path), which is neither the bottleneck Df nor the global cavity Di used in the reported FER/FAU comparisons (E01, E02, E04), so the mapping from those reported cavity-diameter mechanisms to this proxy is a hypothesis, not an established relation. The ratio is dimensionless but its value 1 carries no physical equality threshold: it is a geometric packing proxy only. AV is deliberately not used, since AV is mass-specific fixed-probe accessibility, not molecule-specific free volume, and AV=0 does not imply zero adsorption space.
final_candidate.falsification_criteria: The hypothesis is falsified if, in held-out data, entropy_loss_over_R decreases with Vol/lsd_p**3 when other used inputs are held fixed, or if the descriptor shows no association while competing volumetric measures (e.g., using lsd_f instead of lsd_p) do associate, indicating that the included-along-path sphere is the wrong pore-length scale for configurational confinement. A competing explanation is that entropy loss is governed primarily by rotational (inertia-controlled) rather than volumetric packing effects, in which case a descriptor built from PMI ratios would dominate; also, because lsd_p is Dif and not Di, frameworks with equal lsd_p but different cage topology may have genuinely different confinement, which would show as residual systematic error within strata of equal descriptor value.
final_candidate.proxy_assumptions: Assumes (1) the included sphere along the free-sphere path (Dif) is a usable proxy for the local accessible region governing configurational freedom, acknowledging it is not the global cavity diameter cited in E02; (2) vdW volume of the implicit-H molecule scales with excluded configurational volume; (3) cubic scaling of the sphere volume is geometric, not fitted; (4) the reported cavity-confinement entropy effects transfer conditionally to this benchmark's frameworks and regime. No causal claim: this is an empirical geometric proxy to be tested, and reported source percentages are not embedded as constants.
final_candidate.boundary_behavior: Finite on the full training support: Vol in [20.424, 161.144] angstrom^3 and lsd_p in [3.3452, 15.5604] angstrom, so lsd_p**3 >= ~37.4 angstrom^3 and the ratio is strictly positive and finite (approx. 0.004 to ~4.3 across the training envelope). Neither input has zeros in training, so no legitimate-zero handling issue arises; no imputation is used.

descriptor_candidate.name: vol_to_included_sphere_packing_ratio
descriptor_candidate.hypothesis: If configurational packing confinement dominates the entropy loss for these molecule-framework pairs, then, holding the framework geometry fixed (lsd_p fixed), an adsorbate with a larger van der Waals volume (Vol) excludes a larger fraction of the included-sphere volume along the free-sphere path, leaving fewer accessible positional/orientational microstates in the adsorbed phase and thus a larger entropy loss; and, holding the adsorbate fixed, a framework with a larger included sphere along the free-sphere path (lsd_p) accommodates more positional and orientational configurations, giving a smaller entropy loss. The dimensionless packing ratio Vol/lsd_p**3 is therefore expected to increase with entropy_loss_over_R=(Sgas-Sads)/R.
descriptor_candidate.rationale: Prior descriptors captured linear confinement (GeDi/lsd_p, rotation proxy) and bottleneck cross-section confinement ((SPAN/lsd_f)**2, translation proxy). This descriptor probes the volumetric (three-dimensional packing) degree of confinement: how much of the largest included sphere along the diffusion path the molecule's vdW volume occupies. Vol is a computed vdW volume of the implicit-H molecule, not a measured free volume; lsd_p is the Zeo++ Dif (largest included sphere along the free-sphere path), which is neither the bottleneck Df nor the global cavity Di used in the reported FER/FAU comparisons (E01, E02, E04), so the mapping from those reported cavity-diameter mechanisms to this proxy is a hypothesis, not an established relation. The ratio is dimensionless but its value 1 carries no physical equality threshold: it is a geometric packing proxy only. AV is deliberately not used, since AV is mass-specific fixed-probe accessibility, not molecule-specific free volume, and AV=0 does not imply zero adsorption space.
descriptor_candidate.falsification_criteria: The hypothesis is falsified if, in held-out data, entropy_loss_over_R decreases with Vol/lsd_p**3 when other used inputs are held fixed, or if the descriptor shows no association while competing volumetric measures (e.g., using lsd_f instead of lsd_p) do associate, indicating that the included-along-path sphere is the wrong pore-length scale for configurational confinement. A competing explanation is that entropy loss is governed primarily by rotational (inertia-controlled) rather than volumetric packing effects, in which case a descriptor built from PMI ratios would dominate; also, because lsd_p is Dif and not Di, frameworks with equal lsd_p but different cage topology may have genuinely different confinement, which would show as residual systematic error within strata of equal descriptor value.
descriptor_candidate.proxy_assumptions: Assumes (1) the included sphere along the free-sphere path (Dif) is a usable proxy for the local accessible region governing configurational freedom, acknowledging it is not the global cavity diameter cited in E02; (2) vdW volume of the implicit-H molecule scales with excluded configurational volume; (3) cubic scaling of the sphere volume is geometric, not fitted; (4) the reported cavity-confinement entropy effects transfer conditionally to this benchmark's frameworks and regime. No causal claim: this is an empirical geometric proxy to be tested, and reported source percentages are not embedded as constants.
descriptor_candidate.boundary_behavior: Finite on the full training support: Vol in [20.424, 161.144] angstrom^3 and lsd_p in [3.3452, 15.5604] angstrom, so lsd_p**3 >= ~37.4 angstrom^3 and the ratio is strictly positive and finite (approx. 0.004 to ~4.3 across the training envelope). appended.name: steric_pair_to_included_sphere_ratio
appended.hypothesis: If confinement-driven rotational entropy loss dominates for these molecule-framework pairs, then, holding the framework geometry fixed (lsd_p fixed), an adsorbate with a larger heavy-atom pair distance (GeDi, longest molecular dimension proxy) loses a larger fraction of its gas-phase entropy on adsorption; and, holding the adsorbate fixed, a framework with a larger included sphere along the free-sphere path (lsd_p) imposes a smaller entropy loss. The descriptor GeDi/lsd_p is a dimensionless steric-confinement ratio expected to increase with entropy_loss_over_R=(Sgas-Sads)/R.
appended.rationale: Evidence E02 reports that smaller-cavity zeolites (FER vs FAU) show larger rotational entropy loss, and E01/E04 report larger entropy loss in MFI than FAU. The present inputs do not contain the global cavity diameter Di; lsd_p (Zeo++ Dif) is only the largest included sphere along the free-sphere path and is used here as an empirical proxy for local confinement space, which is a weaker quantity than Di. GeDi is a heavy-atom pair distance in an implicit-H representation, not the full all-atom longest dimension including hydrogens; for single-site molecules GeDi is a legitimate native zero, giving descriptor value 0. This is a proxy combination, not a measured degree-of-freedom count; the descriptor re-expresses existing D0 information rather than adding an observation.
appended.falsification_criteria: The hypothesis fails if, within the training support, pairs with high GeDi/lsd_p do not exhibit higher entropy loss than pairs with low GeDi/lsd_p at comparable AV/ASA (i.e., the apparent relation is explained by accessibility rather than confinement), or if single-site adsorbates (GeDi=0, descriptor 0) do not rank among the lower entropy-loss cases at fixed lsd_p. appended.proxy_assumptions: Assumes lsd_p (Dif, included-along-path sphere) monotonically proxies the local confinement space relevant to rotational freedom, which is not the global cavity diameter Di and not the bottleneck Df. appended.boundary_behavior: Finite training support: GeDi in [0, 10.97181443] angstrom (legitimate native zeros for 54 single-site molecules preserved, giving descriptor 0), lsd_p in [3.3452, 15.5604] angstrom (strictly positive, so the ratio is defined everywhere in the training domain). appended.name: bottleneck_confinement_ratio_sq
appended.hypothesis: If translational/configurational confinement at the framework bottleneck dominates the entropy loss for these molecule-framework pairs, then, holding the framework geometry fixed (lsd_f fixed), an adsorbate with a larger heavy-atom enclosing radius (SPAN) sweeps out a larger excluded volume near the pore windows and its adsorbed-phase translational/configurational freedom is more restricted, giving a larger entropy loss; and, holding the adsorbate fixed, a framework with a larger passing free-sphere diameter (lsd_f) permits more translational mobility, giving a smaller entropy loss. The dimensionless squared ratio (SPAN/lsd_f)^2 is therefore expected to increase with entropy_loss_over_R=(Sgas-Sads)/R. This is a falsifiable conditional statement motivated by the reported FER/FAU and MFI/FAU confinement comparisons (E01, E02, E04), not an established law.
appended.rationale: Proxy limitations: SPAN is a heavy-atom enclosing radius in the implicit-H representation (legitimate zero for single-site species, e.g., 54 training rows) and is not an all-atom molecular size; lsd_f is Zeo++ Df, the largest sphere that can PASS through a periodic free path — a bottleneck diameter, not the global cavity diameter Di (E02's cavity-diameter mechanism must be mapped through this bottleneck proxy explicitly, which is unverified). The square gives a cross-section-like dimensionless ratio (molecular enclosing radius vs. bottleneck radius) but does not preserve any physical equality threshold at 1: SPAN > lsd_f does not prove the molecule cannot transit the pore, because SPAN is a heavy-atom radius about the center of mass while Df is a geometric free-sphere path along the framework. Mechanistically the descriptor couples an adsorbate size/shape proxy with a framework transport-limiting length, targeting the translational side of the reported translational-plus-rotational entropy loss picture (E03). It is distinct from the round-1 descriptor GeDi/lsd_p, which paired a molecular pair-distance with the included-along-path sphere.
appended.falsification_criteria: The hypothesis is falsified if: (1) entropy_loss_over_R does not increase with (SPAN/lsd_f)^2 within frameworks of similar chemistry when other size proxies (Vol, GeDi, MW) are held fixed; (2) the framework bottleneck term adds nothing, i.e., SPAN alone (or lsd_f alone with the adsorbate varied) explains the same variation, indicating the ratio is redundant rather than capturing a confinement coupling; (3) the loss instead tracks the included-along-path sphere lsd_p (cage size) rather than the passing bottleneck lsd_f, supporting a cavity-volume mechanism over a window-bottleneck mechanism.
appended.proxy_assumptions: Assumptions (not established causality): (a) the heavy-atom enclosing radius SPAN is an adequate surrogate for the molecular sweep radius governing translational/configurational restriction in a pore; (b) the passing free-sphere diameter Df is an adequate bottleneck-side surrogate for the confinement length, even though the reported mechanism (E02) used average cavity diameter, which is a different geometric quantity; (c) the confinement-driven entropy-loss mechanism reported for alkanes in MFI/FER vs FAU transfers to this benchmark's molecule-framework pairs at its operating conditions; (d) the squared ratio is a monotone empirical proxy, not a physical cross-section model, and ratio=1 has no threshold meaning.
